text:
anya (docs): Heads-up — I opened a small PR with a converted example for tiered traffic analytics + consumption summary. Not perfect but should be a useful starting point. https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/2345 :eyes:

sam (eng-platform): Saw it, thanks. Quick Q: does the example assume burst credits are normalized per minute or per hour? We need to match the metering docs.

anya (docs): It currently normalizes per minute to match the dashboard query I used. If we want per-hour buckets I can add an alternate snippet.

mike (product): For the UX copy we surfaced in last week's review, we prefer per-hour buckets (aligns with billing periods). Could you add both and label them? One for "hourly" and one for "moving 1m avg" so engineers can pick.

lia (devex): Also flag: the SDK example uses an older header name X-Usage-Tokens. We renamed it to X-RW-Usage in the API change — PR should show new header or call out mapping. I can add a quick snippet for the JS SDK.

anya (docs): Good catch. I will update the header. In the PR I have this sample console export command:

```
# query last hour consumption, aggregated per minute
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-RW-Usage: project=acme,env=prod" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/usage?from=-1h&group_by=1m"
```

sam (eng-platform): That looks fine. A couple of asks: 1) include the Grafana panel link (we have a stable panel id 42) and 2) explicit mention of how burst credits affect the "available" gauge in the dashboard.

anya (docs): Will add panel id and brief note. For burst credits I'm planning a short callout: "Burst credits temporarily extend allowance; panels show consumed vs allocated; billing uses meter reconciliation window (UTC day)." Is that accurate?

mike (product): Accurate but add a line: "Customer-visible allocation is X + burst, where X is committed tier." Keep it short.

lia (devex): For the SDK snippet, propose adding a tiny JS example that uses the new header and shows a 1h vs 1m query return parsing. Something like:

```
// fetch usage, hourly aggregation
const res = await fetch("/v1/usage?from=-1h&group_by=1h", {
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'X-RW-Usage': 'project=acme,env=prod' }
});
const body = await res.json();
console.log(body.series[0].points.slice(-5));
```

anya (docs): Nice. I'll include that under "SDK snippets" section.

sam (eng-platform): One more: add guidance for canary -> stable migration. People often forget to update the quota routing tag and end up double-counting usage. A single-line example showing the routing header (X-Route: tier=canary -> tier=stable) would be helpful.

anya (docs): Good idea. I'll add a short troubleshooting note: "If you see doubled counts, check your routing headers and whether both canary and stable are reporting to the same meter key."

lia (devex): Also add a small code comment that the example dashboard queries use the normalized token units we publish (see docs/units.md). Otherwise people will mismatch totals.

anya (docs): Will add a link to docs/units.md and to Grafana panel 42. Any objections to landing this as a docs PR after I push these edits? I'd like reviewers from eng-platform + product.

mike (product): Go for it. Tag me and sam for review.

sam (eng-platform): Thumbs up. Also consider adding a test prompt set we can run that exercises high token churn — useful for Optimize recommendations. Not necessary for this PR but open a follow-up issue if you don't want to include it now.

anya (docs): I can open a follow-up issue for the test prompt set unless someone wants to draft the TCs now.

deploy-bot: docs-ci started for PR #2345 — build 876 in progress.

anya (docs): Thanks — I'll wait for CI and then ping reviewers. If CI shows linter errors I may re-run in a separate commit.

lia (devex): If you want a tiny extra: add a short note about "quota attribution" when requests hit fallback models (we route to cheaper/compatible variants). That affects per-model meter attribution and customers ask about it.

anya (docs): Good call — I'll add a paragraph: "Fallback routing can change which model meter receives traffic; snapshots in the usage console show per-route breakdowns to help reconcile."

mike (product): Perfect. Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick sync.

anya (docs): PR updated and pushed with the following changes: header rename, JS SDK snippet, Grafana link/panel id, hourly + 1m examples, callout on burst behavior, note on fallback routing, and link to units.md. CI passed. Tagging reviewers now: @sam (eng-platform) @mike (product). :rocket:
